column4: Visit note | 2026-01-28 09:00 AM | Dr. Selina Parvin, Neurology | Patient: Habiba Kabir, 60, female. Mrs. Kabir reports experiencing dizziness whenever she looks up, along with nausea when the spinning sensation occurs. She works as a fisherman and mentions that her symptoms began after recovering from a viral cold in Dhanmondi. She denies any hearing loss, ringing in the ears, or fainting spells. On examination: Dix-Hallpike test positive on the right side, BP 132/86 mmHg, pulse 91 bpm, weight 71 kg. Cranial nerves are intact and coordination is normal. Assessment: Benign paroxysmal positional vertigo. Plan: a prescription was issued. She was advised to get up slowly from bed, avoid sudden head movements, and repeat the Epley manoeuvre at home as shown. Follow-up in 2 weeks.
